newsitem.title: USA: Texas spot power maintains strength in cool temps.
newsitem.headline: Texas spot power maintains strength in cool temps.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) held mostly steady at strong levels again Wednesday in the midst of cool temperatures through the state, industry sources said.
Temperatures throughout Texas were forecast to reach maximums in the high 20s and 30s degrees Fahrenheit Wednesday, then reach the mid-40s on Thursday.
Longer-term forecasts called for colder air to arrive in the state over the weekend, with predictions of temperatures 15 to 30 degrees below normal through early next week.
ERCOT firm, peak power for a 16-hour block for Thursday delivery was talked steady to lower in the $35.00-39.00 range from $36.00-40.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) on Tuesday, brokers and marketers said.
ERCOT electricity for non-firm delivery during Thursday's heavy load hours was notationally assessed down slightly at $33.00-37.00 from $34.00-38.00 per MWh on Tuesday, sources said.

Firm off-peak ERCOT deliveries for Thursday were valued higher at $20.00-22.00 from $18.50-19.50 per MWh on Tuesday, while non-firm delivery during Thursday's light load hours was notionally pegged higher at $17.00-19.00 from $14.00-17.00 on Tuesday, the sources said.
February ERCOT power was valued higher at $32.50-33.50 from $32.00-32.50 on Tuesday, although February peak offers were said to have reached as high as $35.00 in morning discussion.

Separately, Texas Utilities said Wednesday its 1,150 megawatt Comanche Peak nuclear power unit 2 was expected to resume electricity production and synchronize to the grid Wednesday afternoon after shutting over the weekend for the repair of a main feedwater valve.
